text:
While the trade talk swirls around Nikita Kucherov, Jake Guentzel keeps doing the thing he has done his whole career: finishing what his linemates start. He has 13 goals and 27 points in 22 games, two goals in Tuesday's 5-2 win over Washington, and his ice time is up two minutes a night over his last ten games (22.4).

The process is strong. Tampa Bay controls 62.2% of the expected goals at 5v5 with him on the ice, 8.4 points better than without him, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 81st percentile for chances from the home-plate area in front of the net.

The finishing is running hot, though. Thirteen goals on 9.3 expected means a 22% shooting rate (17% last season), and the Lightning have scored 10.7 more goals than expected with him on the ice. Evolving-Hockey also notes he plays with very strong teammates, which flatters raw on-ice numbers. Our range still projects 34 to 51 goals; the middle of that, 42, assumes his shooting drifts back toward normal.
